name: Mineral-pigment mural / cave mural
material: pigments bound on prepared earthen/plaster wall; exact pigments, binders and layer sequence vary by site and period
fabrication_process: allow wall and paint layers to age together
visible_production_marks: brush contour remains integrated with matte wall
transfer/pouncing traces may appear only when evidence supports them
edge_behavior: Paint edges are brush-defined but physically interrupted by plaster grain, cracks and loss; no floating digital vector edge.
mark_making: brush contour remains integrated with matte wall
transfer/pouncing traces may appear only when evidence supports them
color_behavior: Matte mineral/earth palette, local fading and darkening; saturation depends on conservation and period, not a universal sepia wash.
surface_behavior: Pigment film sits on/within a mineral wall ground; cracks, abrasions and losses cross painted forms physically.
composition_behavior: Composition is wall-bound and often hierarchical/serial; respect architecture and iconographic zones instead of treating it as a framed canvas.
structural_limitations: do not invent one universal “Dunhuang palette” across centuries
aging_weathering: aged: localized pigment loss, cracks, soot/dust or abrasion according to environment
museum-conserved: stabilized surface with readable losses
modern reconstruction: clean pigments and wall without fake ancient damage

prompt_fragments.core: Make the image inseparable from a prepared wall: matte pigment, brush contours interrupted by plaster grain, localized loss and aging, and composition designed for architectural surface rather than a floating poster.

evaluation_criteria: wall substrate and paint layer interact
figures obey mural composition rather than photographic depth
scope_note: This module controls material/production behavior. It does not select an era by itself.
